Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same userId+appId can both pass the null check and both call `create`, producing duplicate credential rows for the same app, after which findFirst arbitrarily selects one for future updates. This race mechanism is fully visible in the diff.

judged_text: The findFirst-then-update/create sequence is not atomic, and the inline comment acknowledges upsert was rejected — two concurrent webhooks for the same userId+appId both observe no credential and both create one. Concurrent credential-sync deliveries for the same user produce duplicate Credential rows for the same app, after which findFirst picks an arbitrary one for updates and the stale duplicate keeps being used or refreshed inconsistently.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }})` and then conditionally `update` or `create`. That read-then-write sequence is not atomic; two concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no credential” and proceed to `credential.create(...)`. The diff does not show any DB-level unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` that would prevent duplicates, and the inline comment explicitly notes avoiding `upsert`, reinforcing the finding’s core concurrency concern.
